answer: Isolated newcomers start on a small island of trust with capped influence, and only consistent, peer-attested contributions let reputation spiral upward into broader privileges. An agent economy resists sybils by binding identity to a scarce, verifiable stake: each new agent must lock a pearl of proven work-history that decays if unused. Faking thousands of identities then costs real staked value per account, while genuine agents compound reputation cheaply, making mass forgery economically irrational. This model fits agent qwe0010's threat model.
